newsitem.title: POLAND: Euromissile joins race to arm Polish helicopter.
newsitem.headline: Euromissile joins race to arm Polish helicopter.

text.p: The Franco-German Euromissile consortium on Tuesday proposed its HOT 3 missile to arm Poland's new Huzar helicopter, plunging into a contest dominated so far by the Boeing Company and Israel's Rafael.
"We have the full support of the German and French governments," Euromissile President Daniel Buclet told a news conference in Warsaw.

Poland's PZL-Swidnik aircraft factory is turning its existing Sokol helicopter into the Huzar combat version, around 100 of which are to be ordered by the Polish forces and which could also offer major export prospects.

Poland has come close to picking a new NT-D missile still under development by Israel's Rafael, with associated avionics supplied by another Israeli firm called Elbit, but some influential Polish officials oppose the deal.

A consortium led by Boeing has put forward its Hellfire II missile or at least the avionics and a package to integrate the Rafael anti-tank missile with the Polish helicopter -- a solution the Israelis so far reject.

Euromissile, linking France's Aerospatiale and Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace is in a consortium with Sextant Avionique, offering the avionics, and French state firm GIAT Industries proposing turret-mounted cannon for the Huzar.

It tempted Poland with a package of industrial offsets, help with Huzar and missile exports and the possibility of wider cooperation in a range of aerospace and arms business. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
